full_judgment:
A. T. M, Masud, J.—This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, and the complainant opposite party to show cause why the proceedings in C.R. Case No. 582 of 1975 pending in the Court of Mr. Dauduzzaman Chowdhury, Magistrate, 1st Class, Chittagong, should not be quashed. 

 3. The accused persons surrendered and were enlarged on bail. On 11.11.75 the petitioners filed an application for action under section 253(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code before the learned Magistrate stating, inter alia, that the case land belonged to the Government and that the complainant opposite-party is not in possession of the case land and that the case land was leased out to the petitioners by the Government and that the case is false and frivolous. The learned Magistrate by his order dated 19.11.75 rejected the said petition. The petitioners thereafter moved the Sessions Judge, Chittagong, for making a reference to this Court for quashing the proceedings in the aforesaid case. 

 4. Mr. Abdul Malek, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the Rule submitted that the case land belonged to the Government and the accused petitioners took lease of the same from the Government and are in possession of the same and that the complainant never possessed the said land. He further submitted that the complaint is false and frivolous and as such it is liable to be quashed. He further submitted that in Criminal Motion No. 8 of 1973 the learned Additional District Magistrate Chittagong, held that the complainant is not in possession of the case land and in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 73-74 filed by the complainant it was found by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong, that the case land does not belong to the complainant and that he is not in possession of the same. Mr. Malek also referred to a Police Report dated 25.2.75 showing that the case land was leased out to the accused persons by the Government and they have been put in possession thereof. He further submitted that the complainant instituted Other Suit No. 141 of 1975 in the Second Court of the Subordinate Judge, Chittagong, against the petitioner for declaration of title and consequential relief in respect of the case land. The copies of the order in aforesaid Criminal Motion No. 8 of 1975 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 73-74 and also the copy of Police Report dated 25.2.75 have been filed along with the revisional application before this Court. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submitted that on a perusal of the aforesaid papers in would be apparent that the complainant was not in possession of the case land and accused persons were in possession of the said land after taking lease from the Government and as such no prima facie case has been made out against the accused persons. 

 5. The learned Magistrate after perusing the petition of complaint and examining the complainant on oath was satisfied that a prima-facie case has been made out against the accused persons and he took cognizance of the offence and issued warrant of arrest against the accused persons. 

 6. As regards the allegation under section 379 B.P.C. in the instant case, the learned Magistrate is firstly to decide if the complainant was in possession of the disputed land and if he grew the disputed crops on the said land and then to decide if the accused persons dis-honestly cut and took away the crops without the consent of the complainant. This can be done only on appreciation of evidence produced in support of the allegations. 

 7. The case as sought to be made out on behalf of the accused petitioners is that they having taken settlement of the land from the Government had grown the disputed crops on it but the papers referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioners do not conclusively support such contention. 

 8. It was further submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the complaint is malafide, frivolous and vexatious and that the complainant is litigating over again the same question which has already been decided against him. There is nothing on record to show that the question involved in the present case has already been decided against the complainant by any other competent Court. It is no doubt a well settled principle that where the complaint petition does not disclose any offence a criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed. We have perused the complaint petition in the instant case but we find it difficult to hold that the said complaint petition does not disclose any offence. The allegations made in the complaint petition are required to be tested in the light of the evidence that may be adduced and before that it would be too premature to say that no prima facie case has been made out against the accused petitioners. 

 Having considered the entire facts and circumstances of the case we find no reason to quash the proceedings at this stage.
